guardianfootball.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but…

guardianfootball.title: ‘I suffer a lot’: Villarreal owner Fernando Roig on not enjoying games and the prospect of Liverpool
guardianfootball.description: It will be a tense time for club’s president despite the Champions League game at Anfield offering a symbol of how far they have come The first time Fernando Roig watched Villarreal play as their president, he sat in the stand at a tiny whitewashed ground that had concrete fever and was half empty. It was a Sunday night in the second division, they lost 3-0 to Badajoz, and he didn’t enjoy it much. But then, he doesn’t ever enjoy it much. Even on Tuesday at Anfield, he will not: into his 30th year, the longest presidency in Europe, that is about the only thing that hasn’t changed. More than 1,000 games and still it happens. “I don’t get nervous. It’s worse: I get worried, very anxious,” he…

guardianfootball.title: Wigan pine for FA Cup glory as not even victory can lift them off foot of League One
guardianfootball.description: Gary Caldwell, club captain in 2013 and now manager, needs much more than Saturday’s win over Reading to disperse the clouds If the 2013 FA Cup final represented a blip for the Sheikh Mansour-era Manchester City in their quest for total domination of English football, it was a historic moment for their conquerors, Wigan Athletic. Memories of that famous day at Wembley still endure for Latics’ supporters despite the relegation from the Premier League that followed. Yet watching the modern-day Wigan, who remain bottom of League One despite a 1-0 win over Reading on Saturday, makes the toppling of City in a Cup final seem an epoch ago. The club, perhaps understandably, continue to hark back…

guardianfootball.title: Haaland helps Maresca achieve record start as Manchester City defeat Ipswich
guardianfootball.description: There have been few winners in Manchester City’s guilty verdict, except highly paid lawyers and the inflatable fruit industry. The fans have suffered, being forced to question everything they have been told, while being labelled “cheats”, but they were able to forget the cacophony of noise around the club as Enzo Maresca became the first Premier League manager to win his first seven games. Ipswich were the latest victims, but they put up a fight in City’s first home Premier League game since being found to have breached financial rules . Defiance has fortified most of the City fanbase, who were able to see local boy Phil Foden instigate the triumph with a kiss of the badge, before an…

This was a game with a very clear before and after. Andoni Iraola will hope surviving one of the toughest tests the Premier League has to offer is a sign his methods are starting to work, but Liverpool’s manager will not forget it was a very different contest after Yarmolyuk’s red card for a butt on Jérémy Jacquet left Brentford trying to defend a 1-0 lead with 10 men for the entire second half. guardianfootball.title: Boos at Arsenal as draw with Birmingham extends winless WSL run
guardianfootball.description: An equaliser from Olivia Smith averted defeat for Arsenal, but a home draw with Birmingham did little to calm fears for Renée Slegers’s future as Gunners coach. Boos accompanied the final whistle at the Emirates Stadium, as the result left Arsenal on six points from six matches and without a win in five Women’s Super League matches, the club’s longest winless run in WSL history. They are eighth in the table, nine points behind the leaders, Manchester City, who have played one game fewer. Birmingham opened the scoring at the start of the second half when Océane Hurtré coolly tapped in after her run from the halfway line went unchecked. Alessia Russo had hit the woodwork in the first half…

Divine Mukasa’s first-half strike in front of a record Swansea.com Stadium crowd of 20,973 gave the Hammers a 1-0 win and took them into second place and within a point of the league leaders. It was their second success in four days after a 6-0 romp at Lincoln , and ended a week that began with a 1-1 home draw against QPR following Jarrod Bowen’s last-gasp penalty miss. Continue reading...

pitchfork.title: The Perfect Prescription
pitchfork.description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we investigate J Spaceman and Sonic Boom’s 1987 psychedelic rock album, a mythically drugged-out method of divine transport.

pitchfork.title: DJ-Kicks
pitchfork.description: The UK selector throws caution—and genre—to the winds on an audacious 82-minute set that careens between ambient, drill’n’bass, post-punk, breakcore, and more.

pitchfork.title: Autosmile
pitchfork.description: The Philly duo’s folk music radiates a special kind of energy. Their second album is tinged with psychedelia, a wicker wunderkammer of songs, spells, and secrets.

pitchfork.title: I think I spoke too soon
pitchfork.description: The London pop singer mines the pitfalls of young womanhood for dramedy on her sleeker, more polished second record, finding a sweet spot where goofy melodrama and emotional realism meet.

pitchfork.title: Edge Conditions
pitchfork.description: The Los Angeles synthesist steps out from improvising quintet SML to deliver a playful collection of rhythmic studies, electronic abstractions, and even a wriggly acid jam.

pitchfork.title: Music Is Invisible (Pentimento Volume Three)
pitchfork.description: The final entry in a painting-inspired trilogy of records draws on the trumpeter and composer’s last live show before his death, highlighting his focused, distinctive musical presence.

pitchfork.title: Dopamine Chamber
pitchfork.description: The Irish band’s fifth album balances profound cynicism and genuine beauty as its ice-hearted stadium rock grows to darkly apocalyptic proportions.

pitchfork.title: Purdy
pitchfork.description: The L.A. rapper knows that working artists don’t have it easy. His latest album attempts to reconcile a life of precarity with the spiritual rewards of finding one’s voice.

quietus.title: Organic Intelligence LXI: Electronic Music From Iran
quietus.description: In this month’s antidote to the algorithm, Kamyar Salavati explores the evolution of Iran’s experimental electronic music scene Siavash Amini by Ashkan Norouzkhani I regret not being there, but fellow music critics still remember the shock of buying a ticket for a small concert in central Tehran, only to discover that the artist doing visuals for the electronic musician Sote was none other than Radiohead collaborator Tarik Barr. His Wikipedia photo is from that trip, framed by a detail of the iconic Azadi Tower in the background. This surprising presence was a sign of how the Iranian electronic music scene had gained some remarkable international visibility despite the country’s isolation…

quietus.title: The Avalanches – No Bad Memories
quietus.description: The Avalanches No Bad Memories Avalanches weave a satire on branding and tech enshittification complete with skits by Mike Patton and Haley Joel Osment On arrival, Australian plunderphonics crew The Avalanches only had eyes for record racks, bringing in armfuls of half-forgotten vinyl to harvest for the stunning sampledelic patchwork of 2000 debut album Since I Left You. Then they disappeared for 16 years. In the meantime, they apparently made more friends than music, finally coming back with the collaborator-heavy Wildflower (2016) and the even more convivial We Will Always Love You (2020). They never lost their skill with a sample, but now contributions were equally organic. No Bad…

quietus.title: Orbital Detail New Album, ‘Other’
quietus.description: The duo have also announced an extensive UK and European tour for spring 2027 Photo by Manja Williams Orbital have shared details of a new album, titled Other. Following on from 2023's Optical Delusion, the new record is preceded by lead cut 'Mother, Maiden & Crone'. The song, which you can listen to below, draws on influences from witchcraft and folklore, according to a press release, and features vocals from Maxine Peake. Other is Orbital's 11th studio album, and explores themes of otherness, as the title suggests. It draws on punk, ambient music, drum & bass and the duo's traditional electronic music origins. They will support the album with an extensive tour of the UK and Europe…

I was in the middle of this scene when it…

quietus.description: Both albums have been remastered for their new vinyl pressings Photo by Kirk R. Tuck Butthole Surfers' albums Piouhgd and Humpty Dumpty LSD are being reissued on vinyl. Both have been remastered especially for their updated release, with the audio now available on streaming platforms and vinyl editions set to follow in December. It marks the third set of reissues of the band's material – the two previous ones came in 2024. Originally released in 1991, Piouhgd was Butthole Surfers' fifth album, and was originally released on Rough Trade. Humpty Dumpty LSD, meanwhile, was first released in 2002, and compiled loose ends from the group's mid-80s archival material. Album cut ‘Sherman (Backass…

But, even for her, this has been a particularly busy month. No doubt as much due to the logistical necessities of release schedules as the movement of the stars or artistic intention, October has already seen new albums from two of Magaletti’s other projects: Vanishing Twin (Archives) and Holy Tongue (Basilikum). So I hope she can make a little…

Words & Pics: JR Moores As a wise person once put it, each person delights in the work that suits them best. Some are proficient plasterers, while others practise law. There are sculptors, plumbers, barbers, nurses, mechanics, teachers, chefs and astronauts, all thriving in their vocations. The butcher. The baker. The blockbuster-maker, whose films make a killing at the box office yet leave some viewers feeling colder than Matt Damon’s goolies on the set of Interstellar. The soldier, too, fearlessly travelling to foreign lands where they…

The rapper-producer duo’s abrasive new record serves as a necessary soundtrack for end times i love nature! by Big Flowers x shemar On their new collaborative album, Buffalo-based rapper Big Flowers and NYC producer Shemar offer an unflinching and unfiltered gaze into the chaos of modern life. Equal parts eulogy and battle cry, the record holds a mirror up to a planet heading towards a point of no return. While his previous collaborative record Save The Bees aimed to make sense of the chaotic nature of the world, Big Flowers describes I Love Nature! as “a resistance to our environmental abandonment” referring to the present moment as the “Wall-E grade…

aquariumdrunkard.description: Mid-October approaches, and the owls are not what they seem. The best records belong to a particular hour, season, or state of mind. The soundtrack to David Lynch’s Twin Peaks: Fire Walk with Me seems to exist just beyond all three, somewhere between the last light and whatever waits after dark.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Booker Stardrum :: The Aquarium Drunkard Interview
aquariumdrunkard.description: Jazz grip. Booker Stardrum’s work spans solo recordings, electronic experiments, and collective improvisation. In 2026, he’s released his fourth solo album, Close-up On The Outside , alongside new records with Play Time, OOPS!, Silk Fence, and SML. We spoke with Stardrum about his compositional process and the challenges and possibilities of working across so many different musical settings.

aquariumdrunkard.title: PAINT :: Whip of an Ear
aquariumdrunkard.description: No one is making music quite like PAINT, the project of musician and Allah-Las guitarist Pedrum Siadatian. If a song title can be prophetic, it's "Illusion of Voice" here, in which the vocals of real and hypothetical cast of ensemble characters and collaborators weave through a shadowy labyrinth full of twists of surrealistic transparency. From police blotter audio soundscapes to warbled poetry reads, fourth record Whip of an Ear is an obtusely captivating listen and one of the prolific musician's best offerings yet.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Piero Umiliani :: Il Corpo
aquariumdrunkard.description: Piero Umiliani’s Il Corpo is the sound of something beautiful beginning to sour. Released in 1974, the soundtrack finds the Italian composer in familiar aesthetic territory, where jazz, funk, psychedelia and library music bleed into one another. Sunny music for shady people, it embodies the anything-goes spirit of Italian library music, spinning a parallel film from grooves, fuzz and atmosphere.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Transmissions :: Richard Thompson (2026)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Hippies, Thugs, and Heroes finds guitarist Richard Thompson sounding as savage, lyrical, and eloquent as ever. This week on Aquarium Drunkard Transmissions, we're pleased to welcome Thompson back to the show. If you dig Transmissions, there’s a pretty solid chance that you already know that he's one of the founding fathers of British folk rock, known for his work with Fairport Convention, Sandy Denny, his former wife Linda Thompson, Nick Drake and others.

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Lagniappe Sessions :: Beefheart & McQuinn
aquariumdrunkard.description: Beefheart & McQuinn’s Midtown Downtime arrived earlier this year as a ten-song distillation of folk-rock’s softer, more unhurried pleasures. Think. close harmonies, crisp arrangements, and an easygoing, J.J. Cale-like sway. For their Lagniappe Session, William Murray and Winter McQuinn turn to three favorites from their record collections: Danny O’Keefe’s “The Road,” Mark Fry’s “Song For Wilde,” and Heron’s “Lord & Master.” Spanning road-worn singer-songwriter fare and the pastoral reaches of British folk, the selections share the qualities that animate the duo’s own work.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Sunlight/Water :: A Skygreen Leopards Sampler
aquariumdrunkard.description: Fog lifting off San Francisco’s Victorian rooftops, twelve-string guitars catching the morning light, and the ghost of a California that exists somewhere between memory and myth. A curated sampler spanning Skygreen Leopards’ 2001–2014 catalogue, tracing Glenn Donaldson and Donovan Quinn’s journey from lo-fi jangle-psych fragments to sun-dappled pop reveries—an overlooked gem of the Bay Area underground, steeped in eucalyptus hillsides, coastal haze, and the strange, enduring magic of the West Coast.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Offworlding: Ambient House, 1992-1997 (A Mixtape)
aquariumdrunkard.description: For a fleeting moment in the early-to-mid 90s, ambient house consummated the perfect synthesis of dance music groove and cosmic expanse. Emerging from the chillout rooms and the afterparties at the margins of club culture, ambient house cultivated the psychedelic elements of the rave scene into an altogether more atmospheric direction. The scene produced a handful of genuine superstars in the Orb and the Future Sound of London, but beneath these, there lies a whole galaxy of trippy, pulsing electronica to traverse. Here are a few hours to get you started.

Considered lost for many years, the Faust Bible was recently rediscovered and restored by the Cinématheque, and now MUBI and the Cinématheque have recreated this…

mubi.description: LOOKING THROUGH THE ROOM Blood of Revenge (Tai Katō, 1965). In Blood of Revenge (1965), Hatsue, a young woman bound by contract to a pleasure house, wants to see her dying father. Wearing violet, she bows low to the floor and begs Okatsu, who manages the house, for permission to leave. Okatsu reminds her that she has already been “bought and paid for” and is no longer free to leave on her own. The film’s director, Tai Katō, does not frame the plea as a simple exchange between two people. Hatsue is fully in view, but Okatsu sits deeper in the room, partly screened by translucent fabric. A man leans into the frame from the right. On the left, a woman is just visible in the shadows. She then…

mubi.description: Éric Rohmer in Out 1: Noli Me Tangere (Jacques Rivette, 1971). In 1946, the prestigious French publishing house Editions Gallimard published a novel called Élisabeth by a man named Gilbert Cordier. No one had heard of this Cordier before, or knew anything about him, for the simple reason that he didn’t exist. “Cordier” was a pseudonym adopted by a young teacher of Latin and Ancient Greek from Tulle named Maurice Scherer. When Élisabeth was released to blanket disinterest, Scherer began to branch out from literature into film criticism, and, later, filmmaking. With each new endeavor, the pseudonyms piled up.
